request.question: What is the maximum loan-to-value for a used vehicle?

response.answer:
Relevant policy text (extractive mode, no LLM):
- Loan-to-value (LTV) is the credit amount divided by the collateral value after haircuts. [1]
- Collateral type: New vehicle (up to 1 year old); Valuation basis: Invoice price; Maximum LTV: 90%. [1]
- Collateral type: Used vehicle (1 to 8 years old); Valuation basis: Pricing guide value; Maximum LTV: 80%. [1]

contexts.section: 2. Eligible Collateral and Loan-to-Value Limits > 2.1 Maximum Loan-to-Value
contexts.text:
Loan-to-value (LTV) is the credit amount divided by the collateral value after haircuts. The following maximum LTVs apply at origination:

| Collateral type | Valuation basis | Maximum LTV |
|---|---|---|
| Cash deposit or certificate of deposit held at Meridian Bank | Balance | 100% |
| New vehicle (up to 1 year old) | Invoice price | 90% |
| Used vehicle (1 to 8 years old) | Pricing guide value | 80% |
| Residential real estate, first lien | Independent appraisal | 80% |
| Residential real estate, second lien (home equity) | Independent appraisal | 70% combined LTV |
| Listed equities and exchange-traded funds | Market value | 50% |

Vehicles older than 8 years, cryptocurrencies, art, jewelry and unlisted shares are not eligible collateral.

contexts.doc_title: Personal Loan Limits and Pricing Policy
contexts.text:
Risk grades use the Meridian Risk Score table defined in MB-POL-001 section 3.1.

| Risk grade | Maximum loan amount (USD) | Maximum DTI | APR band |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | 50,000 | 45% | 7.99% to 11.99% |
| B | 35,000 | 45% | 12.00% to 16.99% |
| C | 20,000 | 40% | 17.00% to 23.99% |
| D | 7,500 | 35% | 24.00% to 29.99% |
| E | Not eligible | Not applicable | Not applicable |

The DTI calculation includes the new loan installment. DTI limits may be exceeded by at most 5 percentage points through an approved exception under MB-POL-005.
